summary: Pre-Vote update modeled (MODEL_UPDATED); harness rebased and 18 fresh traces validated; model checking found one real defect (MC-1), reproduced on the updated implementation: a Pre-Vote round survives leader establishment and the new Leader re-elects itself, tripping the leader-vote assertion.
validation_limits: All model checking is bounded (3 nodes, MaxTerm 2, <=2 elections, <=2 Pre-Vote rounds, <=1 crash, <=1 drop, <=5 messages); 30-minute BFS/simulation budgets did not exhaust the state space (LIMITED_COVERAGE).

Traces are engine-level (real Engine methods, runtime command execution emulated by an explicit RuntimeDrain event); RaftCore tick guards, RPC dispatch, and the PreVoteResponse gate as executed in RaftCore are validated by source review, model checking, and the integration reproduction rather than trace replay.
Open focused checks are provisional and budget-limited; the discharge obligation passed only within its BFS budget.

Two prior-model defects were repaired (LogLE on absent logs; leader lease on establishment); prior state counts are not comparable, but with both repairs reverted and Pre-Vote disabled the suite reproduces the prior exhaustive MC.cfg graph exactly.
The Level 3 timer-path reproduction slows save_vote through a test-storage hook (memstore only); the Level 1 reproduction uses only public APIs.

findings.title: Pre-Vote round survives leader establishment and makes the new Leader re-elect itself
findings.cause: A Candidate whose election timer fires starts a Pre-Vote round without dropping its running election; establish_leader clears only `candidate`, so `pre_candidate` survives; handle_pre_vote_resp then calls elect() on the established Leader and do_elect keeps the Leader object.
findings.trigger: Candidate at term T times out (e.g. slow save_vote, or trigger().elect(true) while Candidate) and pre-votes for T+1; the delayed real vote for T arrives first (Leader at T); the granted Pre-Vote reply arrives afterwards.
findings.consequence: The healthy term-T Leader bumps its own term to T+1 while keeping a Leader object at (T, committed); RaftCore::trigger_routine_actions -> try_leader_handler hits debug_assert leader.vote >= state.vote and the core panics (Fatal::Panicked); in release builds the Leader runs behind its persisted vote.

premises: Pre-Vote is enabled (Config::enable_pre_vote or runtime pre_vote(true)) or trigger().elect(true) is called on a Candidate.

The Candidate's own election is still in progress when its election timer fires: e.g. save_vote slower than the election timeout (RaftCore awaits it inline), so queued Ticks run before the vote RPCs are dispatched.
The real-vote reply for term T is delivered before the granted Pre-Vote reply for T+1; both within the vote RPC ttl (election_timeout_min).
No become_following (vote grant to another node, AppendEntries from another leader, role refresh) or restart clears pre_candidate in between.
Debug assertions enabled for the panic consequence (tests); otherwise the stale Leader object persists.

findings.title: Pre-Vote documentation claims an Unreachable response counts as a grant
findings.cause: docs/protocol/pre_vote.md says the default pre_vote returns Unreachable and that Unreachable counts as a grant; the code synthesizes a granting Ok by default and never counts transport errors.
findings.trigger: A peer's pre_vote RPC fails with Unreachable while Pre-Vote is enabled.
findings.consequence: None at runtime: the failed reply is dropped (not a grant), as the repository test pre_vote_unreachable_peer_is_not_a_grant confirms; only the documentation is stale.
